persona: Fundamental equity analyst who screens with precise financials — revenue/EPS growth (YoY, multi-year CAGR, consecutive years), margin levels & trends, ROE/ROIC, FCF & FCF yield, leverage (net debt/EBITDA, debt/equity), absolute-dollar line items, cross-market USD comparisons, and sector-relative 'below/above average' benchmarks. Thinks in specific numbers and multi-condition intersections.

cases.question: Find companies globally with revenue above $5B, gross margin over 60%, operating margin over 25%, and net debt/EBITDA under 1.0x. I want large, high-margin, lightly-levered businesses.
cases.goal: Multi-metric intersection screen: absolute-$ revenue floor + two margin thresholds + leverage ceiling, applied globally.
acceptance: Screen intersects ALL four conditions (revenue $5B AND gross margin >60% AND op margin >25% AND net debt/EBITDA <1.0x) — not a subset
Revenue $5B is treated as an absolute-dollar line item normalized to USD (not local currency, not a ratio)
Net debt/EBITDA uses net debt (debt minus cash), not gross debt/EBITDA
Results are global (no implicit single-country restriction)
Red flag if it returns a raw list and asserts all four filters passed without evidence per metric, or if it silently drops any of the four conditions

cases.question: หาหุ้นที่มีรายได้เติบโต YoY ติดต่อกันอย่างน้อย 5 ปี และกำไรต่อหุ้น (EPS) ก็โตทุกปีในช่วงเดียวกันด้วย ขอเฉพาะบริษัทที่มีรายได้เกิน 1 พันล้านดอลลาร์
cases.goal: Consecutive-years growth screen: revenue up YoY AND EPS up YoY for 5+ consecutive years, with an absolute-$ revenue floor.
acceptance: Interprets 'ติดต่อกันอย่างน้อย 5 ปี' as CONSECUTIVE positive YoY growth for each of 5 years, not merely 5-year CAGR positive
Applies the consecutive-growth condition to BOTH revenue and EPS jointly
Revenue > $1B applied as absolute USD line item
Answers in Thai
Red flag if it substitutes a single 5-year CAGR>0 for the stricter consecutive-year test, or checks only revenue and ignores EPS

cases.question: Compare Toyota, Volkswagen, and General Motors on revenue, net income, operating margin, ROE, and net debt — all in USD so it's apples-to-apples. Which has the strongest balance sheet?
cases.goal: Cross-market head-to-head with explicit currency normalization (JPY/EUR/USD reporting currencies) into USD.
acceptance: Absolute-dollar figures (revenue, net income, net debt) are converted from each company's reporting currency (JPY, EUR, USD) to a common USD basis
Does NOT mix currencies when ranking or comparing absolute magnitudes
Ratios (op margin, ROE) are currency-neutral and can be compared directly without conversion
Provides a reasoned 'strongest balance sheet' judgment grounded in the net debt / leverage figures shown
Red flag if it compares ¥ revenue vs € revenue vs $ revenue as if the numbers were comparable

cases.question: Screen for stocks trading below their sector's average P/E but with ROE above the sector average — cheap relative to peers yet more profitable. Restrict to US large caps.
cases.goal: Sector-relative (cohort) screen combining a below-average valuation condition with an above-average profitability condition, scoped to US large cap.
acceptance: 'Below sector average P/E' and 'above sector average ROE' are evaluated against a cohort/sector benchmark, not against fixed absolute thresholds
The sector benchmark cohort matches each company's own sector (peer-relative), not a single market-wide average blindly applied
Scope restricted to US + large-cap size tier
Both conditions intersected (cheap AND more profitable), not either/or
Red flag if it uses an arbitrary fixed P/E number instead of the sector average, or compares each stock to the wrong cohort

cases.question: I want accelerating growth: companies whose revenue growth rate this year is higher than last year's, and last year's was higher than the year before. So growth is speeding up, not just positive.
cases.goal: Growth-acceleration screen — second-derivative condition on revenue growth over three consecutive periods.
acceptance: Interprets 'accelerating' as growth RATE increasing across periods (g_t > g_{t-1} > g_{t-2}), i.e. rising YoY growth, not just positive growth
Uses at least three growth data points (needs ~4 years of revenue) to establish the acceleration
Does not conflate 'high growth' with 'accelerating growth'
Red flag if it returns companies with high but decelerating or flat growth, or checks only a single growth number

cases.question: Find profitable software companies with free cash flow above $500M, FCF yield above 4%, and net cash on the balance sheet (more cash than total debt). Any market.
cases.goal: FCF-quality + balance-sheet-strength intersection: absolute FCF floor, FCF-yield ratio, and a net-cash structural condition.
acceptance: FCF > $500M is an absolute USD line item; FCF yield > 4% is a ratio (FCF / market cap) — treated as two distinct conditions
'Net cash' correctly means cash & equivalents exceed total debt (negative net debt), not just 'has cash'
Restricts to software/relevant sector and to profitable companies
All conditions intersected globally
Red flag if FCF yield is computed against enterprise value without saying so and then labeled inconsistently, or if 'net cash' is treated as merely having a positive cash balance

cases.question: Show me companies with expanding margins: gross margin, operating margin, and net margin all higher today than they were three years ago. I care about the trend, not the absolute level.
cases.goal: Margin-trend screen — three margin lines each trending UP over a 3-year lookback, level-agnostic.
acceptance: Evaluates the CHANGE (Δ) in each of the three margins over ~3 years, requiring all three to be higher now than 3 years ago
Does not impose an absolute margin threshold (user explicitly wants trend, not level)
Requires all three margins expanding jointly (intersection), not any single one
Red flag if it screens on current margin level instead of the 3-year change, or checks only one margin line

cases.question: ขอบริษัทในเอเชียที่มี ROIC เกิน 15% ต่อเนื่อง, อัตราส่วนหนี้สินต่อทุน (D/E) ต่ำกว่า 0.5 เท่า, และงบดุลแข็งแรง current ratio มากกว่า 2 — เน้นคุณภาพงบดุลและผลตอบแทนจากเงินทุน
cases.goal: Quality + balance-sheet-strength screen scoped to Asia: sustained ROIC, low D/E, strong current ratio.
acceptance: Intersects ROIC > 15% (ideally sustained/multi-year) AND D/E < 0.5 AND current ratio > 2
Scope restricted to Asia (region filter), answered in Thai
ROIC (return on invested capital) is used, not conflated with ROE
D/E and current ratio are treated as currency-neutral ratios (no FX needed)
Red flag if it swaps ROIC for ROE without noting it, or drops the balance-sheet (current ratio) condition

cases.question: Screen for companies with revenue over $10B that spend more than $2B a year on R&D and whose R&D as a percent of revenue is above 15% — heavy, committed innovators at scale.
cases.goal: Absolute-$ line-item screen combining a revenue floor, an absolute R&D-spend floor, and an R&D-intensity ratio.
acceptance: R&D > $2B is an absolute USD line item, distinct from R&D/revenue > 15% which is a ratio — both applied
Revenue > $10B applied as absolute USD
All three conditions intersected; a $2B R&D spender at $60B revenue (3.3% intensity) should be excluded by the 15% intensity gate
Absolute-$ figures normalized to USD across markets
Red flag if it uses only R&D intensity and ignores the $2B absolute floor (or vice versa), or mixes currencies on the dollar line items

cases.question: I'm hunting compounders: 3-year revenue CAGR above 20%, EPS CAGR above 25% (so earnings growing faster than sales — margin leverage), ROE consistently over 20%, and net debt/EBITDA under 2x. Global, any sector.
cases.goal: Full multi-condition compounder screen: CAGR thresholds with a relational EPS>revenue-growth quality condition, sustained ROE, and leverage ceiling.
acceptance: Revenue CAGR > 20% and EPS CAGR > 25% both computed over the same ~3-year window
Captures the relational insight that EPS is growing faster than revenue (margin/operating leverage), not just two independent thresholds — or at least does not contradict it
ROE > 20% treated as sustained/consistent, and net debt/EBITDA < 2x uses net debt
All conditions intersected globally with no implicit sector/country restriction
Red flag if it reports CAGRs over mismatched windows, uses gross debt for the leverage gate, or claims all filters satisfied without per-metric evidence
